name: Picture Analogies
blurb: The first pair goes together. Make the second pair match.
childIntro: The two pictures on top go together somehow. Find the picture that makes the bottom pair go together in exactly the same way.
howItWorks: Pearson describes this as inferring the relationship between two pictures and selecting the picture related to the third in the same way. It runs at OLSAT levels A to C only, because from level D onwards the same reasoning is tested with words instead of pictures.
parentTip: The distractor is almost always something merely associated with the third picture. A kettle goes WITH tea but it is not the opposite of hot tea. Get your child to state the relationship in a full sentence before looking at the answers.

questions.prompt: Which picture completes the second pair?

figure.alt: A cow goes with milk. A bee goes with what?

questions.explanation: A cow gives us milk. A bee gives us honey. A flower is where the bee gets its nectar, not what it gives us.
questions.strategy: Say it as a sentence: a cow gives milk, a bee gives ___.

questions.prompt: Which picture completes the second pair?

figure.alt: A shoe goes with a foot. A glove goes with what?

questions.explanation: A shoe goes on a foot. A glove goes on a hand. A scarf and a coat are clothes but they are not body parts.
questions.strategy: Match the thing you wear to the part of the body it goes on.

questions.prompt: Which picture completes the second pair?

figure.alt: The sun goes with hot. Snow goes with what?

questions.explanation: The sun makes things hot. Snow means cold, and ice is the cold one. A snowman is made from snow and a coat is what you wear in it, but neither one is the feeling of cold.
questions.strategy: Hot and cold. Find the answer that shows the feeling, not the thing that goes with it.

questions.prompt: Which picture completes the second pair?

figure.alt: A caterpillar goes with a butterfly. An egg goes with what?

questions.explanation: A caterpillar grows into a butterfly. An egg hatches into a chick. Choice b skips ahead to the fully grown bird, and the caterpillar to butterfly step is just one step.
questions.strategy: Growing up happens in steps. Move forward the same number of steps.

questions.prompt: Which picture completes the second pair?

figure.alt: A book goes with an eye. Music goes with what?

questions.explanation: You use your eyes for a book. You use your ears for music. A guitar makes music and headphones carry it, but neither is a body part.
questions.strategy: Match the thing to the sense you use for it: eyes, ears, nose, tongue, skin.

questions.prompt: Which picture completes the second pair?

figure.alt: A key goes with a lock. A screwdriver goes with what?

questions.explanation: A key fits a lock. A screwdriver fits a screw. A hammer is another tool, wood is the material, and a builder is the person.
questions.strategy: Tool and the exact thing it works on. Not the material and not the person.

questions.prompt: Which picture completes the second pair?

figure.alt: A fish goes with water. A camel goes with what?

questions.explanation: A fish lives in water. A camel lives in the desert. Choice c is a trap because camels and water are linked in stories, but the pair is about where each one lives.
questions.strategy: Where does it live? That is the whole relationship here.

questions.prompt: Which picture completes the second pair?

figure.alt: Rain goes with an umbrella. Sunshine goes with what?

questions.explanation: An umbrella protects you from rain. Sunglasses protect you from bright sun. An ice cream and a beach go with sunshine but they do not protect you from it.
questions.strategy: Ask what protects you from it, not what you enjoy during it.

questions.prompt: Which picture completes the second pair?

figure.alt: A tree goes with a leaf. A book goes with what?

questions.explanation: A leaf is one part of a tree. A page is one part of a book. Choice b goes the wrong way, from one book to many.
questions.strategy: Whole to part. Make sure you go from the big thing down to the small piece, not up.

questions.prompt: Which picture completes the second pair?

figure.alt: A grown dog goes with a puppy. A grown cat goes with what?

questions.explanation: A puppy is a baby dog. A kitten is a baby cat. Milk and mice are things cats are linked with, and a paw print is something a cat leaves behind.
questions.strategy: Grown up and baby. Every animal has its own baby name.
